project.name: gpsd
project.commit_note: The staged vulnerable checkout under `gt_results/osv_ossfuzz_OSV-2026-189/_work/src` is exactly metadata commit `1c9dd8733a327f9263cb3958904faec029a3497f`. The provided `patch.diff` matches later repository commit `4f56109c04a747a44de37cd345d9d1f8cbc93bf6` (`gpsd/libgpsd_core.c: guard against malicisous fuzzers`), which adds the missing `max_skyview` cap at the crash site; metadata `fix_commit` `1dd9fdb96d2725e9b0eb5e91ff876e065588658b` is unrelated to this function.

bug_description.original: Global-buffer-overflow in gpsd_poll OSS-Fuzz report: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=480975802 ``` Crash type: Global-buffer-overflow READ 1 Crash state: gpsd_poll FuzzDriversStructured.c ```
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `fill_dop()` at `gpsd/libgpsd_core.c:890`, called from `gpsd_poll()` by the OSS-Fuzz target `FuzzDriversStructured`. The exact 8-byte witness selects the structured harness's GeoStar path (`Data[0] % 10 == 3`), producing a valid GeoStar packet with message id `0x22` and one 32-bit payload word `0x20202020`. In project code, `driver_geostar.c` reads that word as `ul1 = 538976288` (`SVs in view`), stores it directly into `session->gpsdata.satellites_visible`, and only then caps the local loop bound `ul1` to `GEOSTAR_CHANNELS == 24` for skyview population. Later `gpsd_poll()` sees `SATELLITE_SET` and a positive `satellites_visible`, so it calls `fill_dop()` with the huge stored count. Vulnerable `fill_dop()` iterates with `for (k = 0; k < gpsdata->satellites_visible; k++)` and never caps `k` to `ROWS(gpsdata->skyview)` (`184`), so after the in-bounds iterations it reaches `k == 184` and line 890 reads `gpsdata->skyview[184].used`, one element past the global `session.gpsdata.skyview[183]` array. The provided patch fixes this exact obligation by computing bounded `max_skyview` before the loop and iterating only to that cap. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image.

source.description: First project statement that consumes attacker-controlled packet content on the crashing path and materializes the `SVs in view` count used later as the unchecked loop bound.
source.value_from: The exact staged 8-byte PoC is `2b ff 22 00 20 20 20 20`. In the structured harness this selects GeoStar (`0x2b % 10 == 3`), message id `0x22`, and one data word `0x20202020`, so this statement reads `ul1 == 538976288` from the admitted GeoStar payload.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. Once `k` reaches the first index past `skyview[183]`, this boolean read dereferences one byte in the global redzone after the `session` object.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `global-buffer-overflow on address ... READ of size 1` at `gpsd/libgpsd_core.c:890:34` in `fill_dop` and says the address is 40 bytes after global variable `session` defined in `FuzzDriversStructured.c:55`.

root_cause.description: The DOP loop uses the attacker-influenced `satellites_visible` field directly as its upper bound and never clamps it to `ROWS(gpsdata->skyview)` before indexing `gpsdata->skyview[k]`.
root_cause.note: The provided patch adds `max_skyview` and replaces this bound with a capped value derived from `ROWS(gpsdata->skyview)`, showing the missing obligation was to bound the loop before any `skyview[k]` access.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant attacker-controlled value is the GeoStar `SVs in view` word parsed from message `0x22`; its raw integer value is later copied into `session->gpsdata.satellites_visible` and reused as the DOP loop bound.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific GeoStar gate. The structured harness-built packet reaches GeoStar recognition and passes the final XOR checksum check, so project packet parsing accepts the witness as a `GEOSTAR_PACKET` before `driver_geostar.c` consumes the `0x22` payload.

fine_trace.note: Source. For the exact staged witness, this reads the sole GeoStar payload word `0x20202020` from admitted message `0x22` and materializes `ul1 == 538976288` as the parsed `SVs in view` count.
The parsed count is copied into persistent session state without validation, so `session->gpsdata.satellites_visible` becomes the huge positive value `538976288`.
A present guard caps only the local loop bound `ul1` to `GEOSTAR_CHANNELS == 24`; it does not repair the already-stored `session->gpsdata.satellites_visible`, which remains `538976288`.

The parser populates at most the first 24 `skyview` entries and sets `SATELLITE_SET`, establishing the satellite-report path that later reaches `fill_dop`. The stored `satellites_visible` from step 2 is not changed here.
Control reaches `fill_dop()` because GeoStar parsing returned `SATELLITE_SET` and the corrupted `satellites_visible` field is a positive integer.

Root cause. The loop bound is the huge propagated `satellites_visible` value, not the actual `skyview` extent. `gpsdata->skyview` has only `MAXCHANNELS == 184` elements (`include/gps.h:2944`), so after the in-bounds iterations `k` still advances and the first out-of-bounds iteration is `k == 184`.

Sink. When step 6 reaches `k == 184`, this reads `skyview[184].used`, one element past the last valid array entry `skyview[183]`. AddressSanitizer reports this exact read as the global-buffer-overflow in `fill_dop`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The provided patch computes bounded `max_skyview` from `gpsdata->satellites_visible` and `ROWS(gpsdata->skyview)` before the loop, then iterates `k < max_skyview`, which directly removes the witnessed out-of-bounds `skyview[k]` read.
sanitizer_ground_truth.source: sample_info.json, reproduction_report.json, sanitizer_trace.txt, exact staged vulnerable source tree, and staged patch.diff; Stage 02 did not perform fixed-image execution.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Not applicable: AddressSanitizer reports a global-buffer-overflow on the global `session` object, so there is no heap or stack allocation context.

format.name: Exact GeoStar structured-fuzzer witness
format.contract: The exact 8-byte witness `2b ff 22 00 20 20 20 20`: byte 0 must select the GeoStar builder (`value % 10 == 3`), bytes 2-3 must form GeoStar message id `0x22`, and the single 32-bit payload word must remain `0x20202020` so project code parses `SVs in view == 538976288` and later reaches `fill_dop()` with that unchecked count.
